messages.subject: Re: geom_rect
parts:
Hi:

I managed to get a background color shading for your plot, but the
variable legend got messed up in the process. Hopefully someone
can rescue that for you.

I did some rearrangement of your plot calls, and created a small data frame to
contain some information for years (I'm assuming 2008-2009, but I could be
wrong...). The following is loosely modeled on the unemployment data graph in
section 5.10, p. 86 of the ggplot2 book.

# Small data frame to contain a factor for which background colors are
# to be mapped, plus a start and end vector of x-values (WEEK). The value
# 5.5 is to provide an illusion of continuity in color - otherwise, there will be a gap
ydata <- data.frame(year = factor(c(2008, 2009)), start = c(1, 5.5),
                    end = c(5.5, 53))

# Removed fill = variable and took out the x-scale
fallplot2 <- ggplot(fallmelt, aes(WEEK, value/1000, linetype = variable,
                    colour = variable)) + geom_line(size = 1) +
                    theme_bw()  +

labs(y="Number of fish (1000s)", x = 'WEEK')

# Modified call - I just reset ymin and ymax so that the color would map
# throughout the y-scale. The values in scale_fill_manual() are what got
# it to work for me, but it messed up the variable legend in the process :(

fallplot2 + geom_rect(aes(NULL, NULL, xmin = start, xmax = end,
    fill = year), data = ydata, ymin = 0, ymax = 20000) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = alpha(c('blue', 'gray50'), 0.01),
                      legend = FALSE)  +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,52,3),labels=levels(fall$week)
                [seq(1,52,3)],)

Hope this is of some assistance.
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: geom_rect
parts: Here's a few more tweaks to get your the whole way:

ggplot(fallmelt, aes(WEEK, value/1000, linetype = variable,
colour = variable)) +
geom_line(size = 1) +

geom_rect(data = ydata, inherit.aes = FALSE, legend = FALSE,
aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, fill = year, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf)) +
scale_fill_manual(values = alpha(c('blue', 'gray50'), 0.1), legend = F)

Note the use of Inf and legend = FALSE in the layer.

Hadley
